intro: Whether you're purchasing a home in Phoenix, Tucson, Mesa, Scottsdale or a smaller Arizona community, understanding your monthly housing expenses can help you choose a property that fits your budget.

Our Arizona mortgage calculator estimates your monthly payment using the purchase price, down payment, mortgage interest rate and repayment period. Include property taxes, homeowners insurance, private mortgage insurance and HOA fees to compare the full housing costs of different properties.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Arizona?

blocks.markdown:
A $400,000 Arizona home purchased with a 20% down payment and a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,918.56.

Arizona offers a diverse housing market, including metropolitan developments around Phoenix, established neighborhoods in Tucson, mountain communities near Flagstaff and retirement communities throughout the state.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Arizona QuickFacts](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/AZ/POP060220), the median value of owner-occupied homes was $394,500 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Homeowners with mortgages reported median selected monthly ownership costs of $1,803. Approximately 67.4% of occupied housing units were owner-occupied.

These historical figures provide context for homebuying decisions, but they should not be interpreted as current listing prices.

Housing costs depend on neighborhood amenities, employment access, property size, construction quality and local demand.

Research the specific city or neighborhood where you intend to purchase before entering a home price into the calculator.

sections.heading: How to Use the Arizona Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Enter the property's expected purchase price and your available down payment.

Select a repayment term and enter the annual mortgage interest rate offered by your lender.

For a more comprehensive estimate, include:

- Annual property taxes.
- Annual homeowners insurance.
- Private mortgage insurance, where applicable.
- Monthly HOA or condominium association fees.

Review the payment breakdown to understand which expenses contribute most to your monthly costs.

You can adjust the inputs to compare a more expensive property with lower association fees against a less expensive property with higher recurring charges.

Use the national Mortgage Calculator to compare financing scenarios outside Arizona.

sections.heading: How Property Taxes Are Calculated in Arizona

blocks.markdown:
Arizona's property taxation system uses several different valuation measures. Understanding them can help you avoid estimating your tax bill using the wrong property value.

### Full Cash Value

Full Cash Value, or FCV, generally represents the assessor's estimate of the property's market value.

However, this figure is not necessarily the value used directly to calculate your annual residential property taxes.

### Limited Property Value

According to the [Maricopa County Assessor's explanation of Limited Property Value](https://www.mcassessor.maricopa.gov/home/understandinglpv/), property taxes for most Arizona real estate are based on Limited Property Value, commonly abbreviated as LPV.

For properties governed by the standard Rule A method, LPV generally increases by no more than 5% annually and cannot exceed Full Cash Value.

Certain property changes can result in a different calculation method.

### Assessed property value

The applicable assessment ratio is applied to the property's limited value before calculating the tax bill.

For example, consider a property with a Limited Property Value of $250,000 and a residential assessment ratio of 10%.

Its limited assessed value would be $25,000.

If the combined hypothetical tax rate were $8 per $100 of assessed value, annual property taxes would equal $2,000, or approximately $166.67 per month.

Actual tax rates, exemptions, levies and charges depend on the property's location.

Review the [Maricopa County Assessor's property tax guidance](https://www.mcassessor.maricopa.gov/faq/property_tax) or contact the appropriate county assessor for property-specific information.

Although Arizona is often associated with dry weather, homeowners face several environmental risks.

Properties in forested communities may be exposed to wildfires, while urban and desert locations can experience monsoon storms, hail and flash flooding.

The [Arizona Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions](https://difi.az.gov/consumers/homeowners-insurance) provides guidance about insurance availability, wildfire exposure and changing premiums.

Obtain insurance quotes before committing to a purchase, particularly if the property is located near wildfire-prone areas.

Standard homeowners insurance generally does not include flood coverage. Use the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) to investigate the property's flood exposure.

Compare coverage limits and deductibles rather than choosing a policy solely because it has the lowest premium.

Include the annual cost of applicable coverage in your mortgage calculator inputs.

sections.heading: Why HOA Fees Matter When Buying an Arizona Home

blocks.markdown:
Many planned residential developments, condominiums and retirement communities have homeowners associations.

HOA charges may support community landscaping, swimming pools, shared facilities, security or maintenance.

Although these expenses are often paid separately from the mortgage, they affect how much money you need each month.

Consider two properties with identical mortgage terms:

- Property A has monthly HOA dues of $75.
- Property B has monthly HOA dues of $300.

Property B would cost an additional $225 each month, equivalent to $2,700 annually, even if the purchase prices were identical.

Review association financial statements, reserve funds, governing documents and potential special assessments before purchasing.

A low monthly HOA fee does not necessarily mean the association has sufficient funds for future repairs.
These illustrative examples assume a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year loan term.

Property taxes, homeowners insurance, PMI and association dues are not included in these figures.

Adjust your calculator inputs using the actual expenses associated with each home.

Arizona homebuyers who have sufficient income to support mortgage payments but limited upfront savings may benefit from down payment assistance.

### Home Plus down payment assistance

The Arizona Industrial Development Authority's [Home Plus program](https://homeplusaz.com/arizona-dpa-programs/) offers qualifying homebuyers assistance of up to 4% toward down payment and closing expenses.

The program combines assistance with an eligible first mortgage. Its second mortgage can be forgiven after 60 months, subject to program requirements.

Applicants must satisfy applicable income, lending and homebuyer education requirements.

Compare the complete financing terms with other available mortgage options.

### Arizona Is Home program

Arizona Is Home is another assistance initiative, but funding availability is limited.

According to the [program administrator's October 2026 update](https://homeplusaz.com/home-plus-dpa-lender-support/), its 2026 allocation was exhausted on October 6.

Buyers should check the official website for future funding announcements rather than assuming assistance remains available.

Do not include unapproved assistance in your home purchase budget.

sections.heading: Types of Mortgages Available in Arizona

blocks.markdown:
Conventional mortgages may suit buyers who meet standard lender requirements.

FHA-insured financing offers another option for eligible borrowers who have limited savings or need more flexible qualification criteria.

Veterans and qualifying service members may consider [VA home loans](https://www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans/), while buyers in eligible rural communities may investigate [USDA housing programs](https://www.rd.usda.gov/).

Borrowers purchasing properties that require specialized financing should verify property eligibility with their lender before making an offer.

Compare estimated monthly payments, mortgage insurance, closing costs and long-term interest expenses across programs.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning a Home in Arizona

blocks.markdown:
Your mortgage payment represents only part of the financial commitment associated with homeownership.

### Electricity and cooling

Air conditioning can be a significant expense during Arizona's hotter months.

Request historical electricity bills and inspect the age and condition of the property's cooling equipment.

An older or poorly maintained system may increase operating costs or require expensive repairs.

### Water and landscaping

Outdoor landscaping, swimming pools and irrigation systems can increase household water usage.

Consider the ongoing costs of maintaining these features, especially when comparing properties with different lot sizes.

### Property maintenance

Roofing, exterior surfaces, plumbing and cooling systems can require periodic repairs or replacement.

Maintain an emergency savings reserve instead of committing every available dollar to your down payment.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Arizona?

blocks.markdown:
Calculate your available monthly income after taxes and regular expenses.

Our [Arizona Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/arizona-paycheck-calculator/) can help you estimate take-home pay. You can also use our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate existing debt obligations alongside a proposed mortgage payment.

Include realistic cooling, transportation, insurance and maintenance expenses before deciding how much you can spend.

Compare lender offers using the [CFPB's mortgage shopping resources](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/), and remember that a loan approval does not guarantee that the payment will be comfortable for your household.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $400,000 Arizona home?

With a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year loan term, principal and interest would be approximately $1,918.56 per month. Your total housing expenses depend on taxes, insurance and applicable association fees.

### Are Arizona property taxes based on the home's purchase price?

Not directly for most residential properties. Arizona generally uses Limited Property Value and an applicable assessment ratio when determining taxable assessed value. Contact the local county assessor for an accurate property-specific estimate.

### Can Arizona homebuyers receive down payment assistance?

Yes. Eligible buyers may qualify for programs such as Home Plus. Assistance amounts, mortgage conditions and eligibility requirements vary. Confirm current terms with a participating lender.

Use our Arizona mortgage calculator to compare different purchase prices, loan terms and down payments.

Include property-specific insurance, taxes and association fees whenever possible. A comprehensive monthly estimate makes it easier to find an Arizona home that fits both your immediate budget and long-term financial goals.
